articles.title: Russian arrested for spying on US defence company Palantir over Ukraine support
articles.summary: The suspect followed employees and was found with fake US IDs and two Russian passports, prosecutors say.
articles.body: The alleged foreign agent was discovered with two Russian passports A Russian man has been arrested in California's Silicon Valley for allegedly attempting to spy on employees of a technology and defence firm that supports the Ukrainian military. Igor D'iu is accused of acting as an agent of a foreign government to conduct a covert operation in Palo Alto, near San Francisco. The BBC understands that the company targeted was Palantir Technologies. D'iu is also charged with stalking employees and possessing falsified identity documents. The company is not named in charging documents, but is described as a publicly traded technology and defence company that produces software used by Ukraine in its war with Russia. "The allegations in this case describe a state-sponsored operation to target and harass employees of an American technology and defense company because of that company's assistance to Ukraine in its war with Russia," said US Attorney for the Northern District of California Craig Missakian. "We will not tolerate any efforts - by foreign governments or otherwise - to turn Silicon Valley into a base for foreign intelligence operations." Prosecutors say that D'iu entered the US unlawfully via the Mexico border, after travelling there from Istanbul in June. He was allegedly recruited through the Telegram encrypted messaging app. His handlers referred to Russia as "'the Motherland' and directed D'iu to gather information about the company because it was supplying weapons used against Russia in Ukraine". On their instruction, he purchased computers, phones, wireless networking equipment and remote access software - tools he needed for his spy mission. He then went to a coffee shop located near the company's offices in Palo Alto, where he photographed laptop screens of employees who were working there. His handlers also allegedly "instructed him to position his laptop at designated locations near the company so they could remotely access it and attempt to collect information from company employees in the vicinity". The suspect allegedly took photos of employees screens at a cafe near the office A source in the industry confirmed that Palantir was targeted, and added that the operation did not penetrate the company's private systems. They added that the company has been "targeted extensively" by Russia over its involvement in Ukraine, and that the attacks are becoming "increasingly aggressive". The source, who did not want to be named, said that this was the first time a Russian operative was found while on US soil attempting to spy on the company. "I think the surprising thing is that they decided to take the risk of sending someone to the US," they said, in an attempt to get into the system "physically". On 3 September, he followed a vehicle driven by one senior executive for nearly 30 miles. He fled after she drove to a police station. Police later obtained evidence that he had followed other employees' cars on previous days. During the investigation, officials discovered identity cards that had been falsified - including a US passport, California ID card, and a Social Security card with the fake name "Hugo Landry Johns". A raid on his home in October in East Palo Alto turned up two Russian passports, and a handwritten notebook that contained numerous home addresses of employees "family members' names, educational and employment histories, and assessments of their strengths and weaknesses", prosecutors say. He faces two charges related his alleged work as a foreign agent, one charge of interstate stalking, and one count of fraud related to his identity documents. He faces over 15 years in prison if found guilty. The suspect was found with forged identification documents including a US passport Ukraine's long-range drones using Western tech to hit Russia He has been held in jail since 2 November. It is unclear whether he has hired a lawyer who can speak on his behalf. Palantir, which was co-founded by billionaire Peter Thiel, has interests in US defence and security, and has contracts with the Israeli military. The arrest comes as espionage allegations roil the US tech industry, amid the news that Nvidia ex-CEO Jensen Huang had a romantic affair with a woman suspected of spying for China. Last month, a former OpenAI employee was charged with planting a listening device in a company office. The man was later accused of having "considerable support" from the Saudi government. articles.title: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war with Russia
articles.summary: Watch: The BBC's Jonathan Beale joins Ukrainian forces taking the battle below ground and out of sight of Russian drones.
articles.body: For the past seven months Ukrainian forces have been living and fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet gas pipeline in the Kharkiv region. The BBC is the first international broadcaster to enter the pipeline where this subterranean battle is taking place. With a diameter of just over a metre there's enough room only to crawl. But it is relatively safe from the drones that now saturate the skies above the front line – and which are making it nigh-on impossible for either side to advance. The BBC's defence correspondent Jonathan Beale reports from near Kupyansk, where he went underground with the 13th Khartiia Operational Brigade.

What the Crimean bridge attack means for Russia
articles.summary: Ukraine's latest strike on the Kerch Bridge has disrupted a key transport link between Russia and Crimea. Beyond the damage, the attack could have serious consequences for Russian military logistics and Putin's prestige.
articles.body: It had been a year and a half since Ukraine last attacked the 19-kilometer-long Kerch Bridge connecting Russian-annexed Crimea with Russia's Krasnodar region. Now, Ukraine has struck again. The attack during the night of November 17 caused the highway section of the bridge to collapse into the sea. As a result, shipping traffic between the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov has also been disrupted. Russia's ministry of transport announced a "temporary suspension" of road and rail traffic on the bridge, though later, rail services were resumed. Russian authorities have launched a criminal investigation into what they are calling a "terrorist attack." It was only after this announcement that the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) confirmed the attack. The Kerch Strait bridge is considered one of Russian President Vladimir Putin's most prestigious projects. Its construction began after Russia's 2014 annexation of the Ukrainian Crimea peninsula , an act considered illegal under international law. The Kerch Bridge was completed four years later. It has been targeted by Ukraine on several occasions since Russia's 2022 full-scale invasion . The most well-known strike occurred in October 2022, when an explosives-laden truck detonated on the bridge, causing extensive damage and several months of traffic restrictions. The most recent attack took place in June 2025, when the SBU reported that an underwater support structure was blown up. The latest Ukrainian operation lasted about a month, and consisted of seven distinct phases. "First, the SBU and armed forces systematically neutralized the enemy's air defense system. After that, the direct attack on the bridge began," says the SBU Telegram channel. Some Russian military bloggers claim that the attack was carried out with the support of Ukraine's Western allies, or at least using their equipment and weapons. Ukraine has not confirmed this. It has instead pointed out that various Ukrainian-made weapons were used in the attack, ranging from a variety of drones, to FP-5 Flamingo and R-360 Neptun missiles. British daily The Times has cited Ukrainian military sources, saying that Ukraine attacked the bridge without the support of SpaceX's satellite network system Starlink . There has been no confirmation of this so far. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy , meanwhile, described the strike as a response to Russian attacks: "Russia is attacking our infrastructure every day, particularly bridges in Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro, Kyiv, and the Odesa region." He said "we are rebuilding our infrastructure, but we also remind Russia that the war always returns to where it began." To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video After the attack, pictures and videos of the bridge were shared on social media. The Krimskij Veter Telegram channel has highlighted damage to the railroad link and questioned why Russian authorities have opted to resume train services. The Kerch Strait shipping channel is also completely blocked by debris. "This brings road traffic to a standstill, but also shipping between the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov," the channel writes. Indeed, the Kerch Strait navigational channel is merely 120 meters wide, writes Mychajlo Hontschar of the Ukrainian Center for Global Studies "Strategy XXI" on Facebook. "The strait is shallow, only three to five meters deep." As early as the 19th century, the seabed was dredged to allow heavier ships to pass from the Black Sea to the Sea of Azov and vice versa. "Now, Vladimir Putin's bridge-building efforts have brought shipping to an indefinite standstill," Hontschar said. Not only will river-sea vessels no longer be able to leave the waters of the Sea of Azov, the Don, and the Volga, but boats and small ships from the Black Sea fleet and the Caspian flotilla based in Novorossiysk will also be unable to do so. Many pro-Kremlin Telegram channels have been quick to claim that the bridge does not play an important role in the Russian army's logistics or in supplying Crimea. The Dva Mayora (Two Majors) channel quotes the "Deputy President of the Republic of Crimea," Olga Kurlayeva, who described the bridge as a "purely civilian structure." Ukrainian military experts interviewed by DW, on the other hand, point to the systematic disruption of Russian logistics. These efforts also included regular attacks on the R-80 highway leading through Russian-occupied territories of the Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, and Kherson regions. Russia cannot replace the Kerch Bridge with any other land connection, says Oleksandr Kovalenko, a Ukrainian military expert with the Information Resistance Group that seeks to counter disinformation. He expects the damaged bridge will cause supply problems for the Russian armed forces: "If there is a resource shortage during attacks or in defense, then either the attacks or the defense will fail." That is why he does not rule out a decline in attacks from occupied Crimea on the rest of Ukraine. "There are many launch pads for kamikaze drones in Crimea — in the Hvardijsk area, at Cape Chauda and in Balaklava," Kovalenko told DW. "From there, many drones are launched toward Odesa, Mykolaiv, and the right bank of the Dnipro River in the Kherson region. They also fly over Crimea en route toward Ukraine. Then there are attacks using Iskander-M ballistic missiles, as well as Zircon and Oniks missiles, guided missiles, and glide bombs. And while they don't originate in Crimea, they are brought over via the Kerch Bridge." Kovalenko says the bridge strike has dealt a serious blow to Vladimir Putin's standing. It comes at a sensitive time as Putin is about to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, China . Memes and witty comments about the bridge abound on X. Meanwhile, the Russian president's spokesperson Dmitry Peskov has promised to rebuild the bridge and assured that it will be "even better than before." Andrii Korezkyj of the Kyiv University of Transportation, however, says this is not likely to happen anytime soon. "All in all, I would estimate that it would take between one and a half and three years [to rebuild]," Korezkyj told DW, adding, "I don't think they'll let the Russians build another [bridge] arch like that near the Ukrainian border without interference." Pro-Russian commentators, known as Z-bloggers, agree with this view. "Unlike in 2022 and 2023, the Ukrainian armed forces are now able to launch strikes against floating cranes and repair teams." "Even installing a pre-assembled arch under these conditions would constitute a challenging task," writes the pro-Kremlin Rybar Telegram channel.

Kuwait says it repelled first Iranian attack in two months after US strikes island
articles.summary: Bahrain says it was also attacked by Iran following a US air strike on the Iranian island of Qeshm in the Gulf on Tuesday.
articles.body: Kuwait condemned the attack, which Iran said targeted an airbase hosting US forces (file photo) Kuwait and Bahrain have said they repelled Iranian air attacks overnight as hostilities between Iran and the United States rise. The drone attack on Kuwait was the first in more than two months. The Iranian army said it had targeted the Ali Al Salem Airbase, which hosts US forces, but Kuwaiti authorities did not report any damage. It came after US warplanes struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, according to US military officials. Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates' state oil firm said a crew member was missing after one of its tankers was attacked in the Gulf waterway on Tuesday. The recent exchanges of fire, as well as deadlock in negotiations on a peace deal, have raised fears of a major escalation in the nine-month-old war. The conflict began when the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February. Since then, Iran has retaliated for US and Israeli strikes by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel. It has also attacked dozens of commercial vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass. Pakistani man sentenced to 27 years for Iran-backed plot to kill Trump Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against Washington On Tuesday night, Kuwait's military said its air defences engaged "drone threats" but did not report any casualties or damage. The Kuwaiti foreign ministry condemned the attack, saying it "flagrantly violated Kuwait's sovereignty, directly threatened its security and stability, and constituted a grave breach of international law". "The explosions seemed to be coming from far away, but hearing them again after a period of calm was both surprising and worrying," Hani Mohammed, an Egyptian resident of Kuwait, told AFP news agency. Bahrain's military also said on Wednesday that its air defence systems had "intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks". The island kingdom, which hosts the US Navy's 5th Fleet, has reported four attacks over the past six days, following a two-month lull. Qatar, which has mediated in the stalled indirect talks between Iran and the US, said the Iranian attacks on its neighbours were a "dangerous escalation that threatens to complicate efforts aimed at containing tensions". The Iranian army said its drones had targeted US Patriot air defence systems and drone and missile launch platforms at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait. Later, the army's commander-in-chief, Maj Gen Amir Hatami, warned the US and its allies that it would respond more forcefully to any new attacks on Iran. "If the enemy repeats its mistake... we have the readiness and the plans to confront it and its supporters in a stronger, more crushing way and without geographic limitations," he said. On Tuesday night, US fighter jets targeted a missile launch site on Qeshm Island "with precision munitions" in response to Iranian "aggression targeting US personnel and assets", US military officials said. Iranian media reported explosions on the island but cited a local official as saying they had caused no damage to infrastructure. In a separate development, the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (Adnoc) said a search-and-rescue operation was under way for a missing sailor following an attack on one of its vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday. The rest of the crew were safely evacuated and 11 were receiving medical care, it added. The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) centre reported that a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile about 13 nautical miles (24km) north of Khasab, in Oman's Musandam peninsula. It said the attack caused a fire on board that was extinguished. Iran said two oil tankers and a ship carrying liquefied natural gas (LNG) had caught fire after hitting naval mines while sailing along an "authorised route". At least 25 seafarers have been killed across the Middle East since the start of the war, when the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed due to Iranian missile and drone attacks on commercial vessels and a US naval blockade of Iranian ports. The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the conflict and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade. Iran insisted it would not give up some measure of control over the waterway and began targeting vessels using a southern route through Omani waters that avoids its preferred route through Iranian waters. In recent months, the US military has been providing protection for tankers shuttling through the Strait of Hormuz, allowing crude oil exports from Gulf states to reach around 80% of pre-war levels, according to analysts.

Hearing on "Georgian Dream's" lawsuit to ban five opposition parties resumes today in the Constitutional Court
articles.summary: The hearing in the Constitutional Court on "Georgian Dream's" lawsuit regarding the ban of five opposition parties will resume today, November 19, at 12:00 PM. Today's proceeding continues in a question-and-answer format, with the plaintiff side continuing to ask questions.
articles.body: The hearing in the Constitutional Court on "Georgian Dream's" lawsuit regarding the ban of five opposition parties will resume today, November 19, at 12:00 PM. Today's proceeding continues in a question-and-answer format, with the plaintiff side continuing to ask questions. For context, the review of the lawsuit in the Constitutional Court began on October 21. The case is being heard by a plenum of seven Constitutional Court judges. The lawsuit submitted to the Constitutional Court is signed by 88 members of Parliament. Based on their lawsuit, the question of declaring the following five political associations unconstitutional is on the court's agenda: "Unity – National Movement"; "Coalition for Change – Gvaramia, Melia, Girchi, Droa"; "Strong Georgia – Lelo, For the People, For Freedom!"; "Federalist Party"; and the party "Gakharia For Georgia." Attached to the constitutional lawsuit is the conclusion of the temporary investigative commission formed in the 11th convocation of Parliament.

articles.title: Paata Manjgaladze: I appeal to Ms. Eva Gotsiridze and other judges of the Constitutional Court – do not accuse me of what not even the state prosecution charges me with
articles.summary: Imprisoned politician Paata Manjgaladze appeals to the judges of the Constitutional Court, including Judge Eva Gotsiridze, "not to accuse him of what not even the state prosecution charges him with." As Paata Manjgaladze explains, not only was he not the organizer of the October 4 rally, but the Prosecutor's Office does not even charge him with any crime provided for by the Criminal Code against…
articles.body: Imprisoned politician Paata Manjgaladze appeals to the judges of the Constitutional Court, including Judge Eva Gotsiridze, "not to accuse him of what not even the state prosecution charges him with." As Paata Manjgaladze explains, not only was he not the organizer of the October 4 rally, but the Prosecutor's Office does not even charge him with any crime provided for by the Criminal Code against the constitutional order and the foundations of national security. Let us respect the presumption of innocence protected by the Constitution, and I ask you, do not accuse me of what not even the state prosecution charges me with. Furthermore, I hereby explain that not only was I not the organizer of the October 4 rally, but the Prosecutor's Office does not even charge me with any crime provided for by the Criminal Code against the constitutional order and the foundations of national security. The charges against me are built on statements made in October 2024, one year prior to October 4, 2025, which is evidence not of my guilt, but of a crime committed jointly by the court and the Prosecutor's Office. Regarding my innocence, please familiarize yourselves with the Public Defender's amicus brief, as well as the assessments of the Georgian Young Lawyers' Association and Transparency International. And finally: I also ask you not to resemble the Sanhedrin known from the Gospel—the accusers of Christ—one of whose elder members even tore his garments out of joy when he supposedly received evidence of blasphemy from Christ," Paata Manjgaladze 's appeal states.

articles.title: Papuashvili: Until the EU Ambassador personally condemns the attack on the Presidential Palace, I will not stop reminding him
articles.summary: Georgian Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili has accused the European Union's ambassador to Georgia of failing to explicitly condemn the October 4, 2025, attack on the presidential palace, claiming that the diplomat's silence amounts to support for those involved. Papuashvili said he had written to the EU ambassador asking him to condemn violence but had received no direct response addressing the incident.
articles.body: Georgian Parliament Speaker Shalva Papuashvili has accused the European Union's ambassador to Georgia of failing to explicitly condemn the October 4, 2025, attack on the presidential palace, claiming that the diplomat's silence amounts to support for those involved. Papuashvili said he had written to the EU ambassador asking him to condemn violence but had received no direct response addressing the incident. “I have also written to the EU ambassador, asking him to condemn violence, but to this day he has not condemned a single act of violence. The only thing he throws back at us, as if we were in kindergarten, is a general statement: ‘The European Union condemns violence.’ Where does it condemn it? In Australia, Antarctica or the Arctic? We need a direct answer on whether he condemns the October 4, 2025, storming of the Presidential Palace! Until he says these words, he is a supporter of this attack and a defender of those who took part in it,” Papuashvili said. On October 4, 2025, demonstrators gathered in central Tbilisi during local election day protests, with some attempting to enter the Presidential Palace. The incident escalated into clashes between protesters and police. Georgian authorities described the events as an attempted overthrow of the government, while several participants were arrested in connection with the incident. The EU has repeatedly expressed concern over developments in Georgia, including restrictions on protests and the use of force against demonstrators. In 2026, plea agreements were reached with dozens of individuals at various stages in connection with the October 4, 2025 events. Crimea Bridge reportedly targeted in third consecutive attack
articles.summary: Explosions were reported near the Crimean Bridge, also known as the Kerch Bridge, overnight on November 19, marking the third consecutive day of reported attacks on the strategically important crossing linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula.
articles.body: Explosions were reported near the Crimean Bridge, also known as the Kerch Bridge, overnight on November 19, marking the third consecutive day of reported attacks on the strategically important crossing linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula. Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty reports that the first reports of the latest attack emerged from the pro-Ukrainian Telegram channel Krymsky Veter, which monitors developments in Russian-annexed Crimea, and the Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova+. At approximately 2 a.m., a message published on the Telegram channel of Sergei Aksyonov, the Russian-installed head of Crimea, stated that traffic across the bridge had been temporarily suspended following another attack and that an assessment of the damage was underway. Sources cited by Krymsky Veter claimed that the railway section of the bridge had been targeted in a missile strike. However, the report has not yet been independently verified. The latest incident follows Ukrainian drone and missile strikes against the bridge on November 16 and 17. Ukraine's General Staff reported that powerful explosions had severely damaged the crossing, claiming that its road section was no longer operational, one of its arches had collapsed, and an arch supporting the railway section had also sustained damage. On November 17, Russia's Ministry of Transport announced that railway traffic had resumed on one of the bridge's two tracks, while repair work continued on the second. The Crimean Bridge has been repeatedly targeted by Ukrainian forces since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Among the most significant previous attacks were explosions in October 2022 and July 2023, which caused extensive damage to the crossing. Another explosion was reported in June 2025. The bridge, which spans the Kerch Strait, was constructed by Russia following its illegal annexation of Crimea in 2014. Its road section opened in 2018, followed by the railway section in 2019. The crossing serves as a major transport connection between mainland Russia and the occupied peninsula and has considerable strategic and symbolic importance for Moscow. Ukraine considers the bridge, which it regards as illegally constructed, a legitimate military target because of its role in supporting Russian operations. The full extent of the damage caused by the latest reported attack remains unclear.

articles.title: War Criminal Dragomir Milosevic Stays in Prison: Request for Release Denied
articles.summary: The President of the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT), Graciela Gatti Santana, rejected a request for early release of Dragomir Milošević, the wartime commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps of the Army of Republika Srpska (VRS), sentenced to 29 years in prison for terrorizing the citizens of Sarajevo.
articles.body: The President of the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT), Graciela Gatti Santana, rejected a request for early release of Dragomir Milošević, the wartime commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps of the Army of Republika Srpska (VRS), sentenced to 29 years in prison for terrorizing the citizens of Sarajevo. The decision was made on November 16, and its public version was published today on the Mechanism’s website. Estonia initiated the procedure, and Milošević has been serving his sentence since March 2011. On July 3, Estonian authorities informed the IRMCT that, according to their law, Milošević became eligible for consideration for conditional release as of August 20. “The high gravity of his crimes goes strongly against granting him early release,” Gatti Santana said, adding that Milošević did not accept responsibility for what he had done. Iz odluke se vidi da puštanje nisu preporučile ni estonske zatvorske vlasti. One Miloševića ocjenjuju kao osobu visokog rizika za društvo, a vjerovatnoću da ponovo počini krivično djelo procijenile su na 15 posto. Nakon izlaska iz zatvora planirao je živjeti u Srbiji, ali je mjesto u javnoj verziji odluke zatamnjeno. The decision reveals that the release was not recommended by the Estonian authorities. They assessed Milošević as a high-risk individual to society and estimated the probability of him reoffending at 15 percent. Upon release, he planned to live in Serbia, though the specific location is redacted in the public version of the decision. In his request, Milošević admitted that the crimes he was convicted of are extremely grave and cited his 2024 statement in which he claimed to fully accept responsibility. He claimed he has never, neither publicly nor privately, challenged the Hague Tribunal, and that his rehabilitation cannot be assessed based on one conversation from February 2024. The IRMCT President did not accept this. As she said, Milošević described his role as a failure to prevent his subordinates, which does not align with the verdict convicting him of both ordering shelling and conducting a campaign of terror against civilians. Milošević also claimed that a prison report does not reflect his true medical condition. He cited a doctor who wrote in 2025 that an early release was medically justified and requested an expert evaluation of two medical incidents, one from 2025 and another from July of this year. In her decision, Gatti Santana notes that the same doctor confirmed in that very same report that the medical care in prison is adequate and that Milošević is capable of taking care of himself. In Milošević’s favor, the President took into account his good behavior in prison, with no rule violations or disciplinary measures, as well as the fact that upon release he would have family support along with his and his wife’s pensions. Nevertheless, as she noted, “good behavior in prison is merely the minimum expected of a convicted person.” Gatti Santana se konsultovala sa sudijama Liu Daqunom i Ivom Nelsonom de Caires Batista Rosom, koji su se obojica složili da zahtjev treba odbiti. Gatti Santana consulted with the judges Liu Daqun and Ivo Nelson de Caires Batista Rosa, both of whom agreed that the request should be rejected. This is the fourth time that the IRMCT has rejected Milošević. His request was rejected in July 2020 because he had not yet served two-thirds of his sentence, then in December 2024 because of the gravity of the crimes and insufficient signs of rehabilitation, and in 2025 when he requested early release for humanitarian reasons. He completed two-thirds of his sentence in March 2024. In December 2007, the Hague Tribunal sentenced Milošević, former commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps of the VRS, to 33 years in prison for terror against civilians, murder, and inhumane acts during the siege of Sarajevo. In November 2009, the Appeals Chamber reduced his sentence to 29 years, Klix ..ba writes.

articles.title: Gorduladze: Gvaramia called detainees political prisoners, Gakharia described protests as peaceful, Saakashvili said ‘I am proud of each and every one of you’
articles.summary: Archil Gorduladze, chair of the Parliament's Legal Affairs Committee, presented public statements made by opposition politicians in 2023 and 2024 during proceedings at the Constitutional Court. He said opposition representatives had portrayed violent protests as peaceful demonstrations and described detained individuals as political prisoners.
articles.body: Archil Gorduladze, chair of the Parliament's Legal Affairs Committee, presented public statements made by opposition politicians in 2023 and 2024 during proceedings at the Constitutional Court. He said opposition representatives had portrayed violent protests as peaceful demonstrations and described detained individuals as political prisoners. Gorduladze recalled a November 27, 2024, statement by Nika Gvaramia, leader of the Coalition for Change, at a joint press conference with members of the European Parliament in Strasbourg. Gvaramia called for the release of several detainees, naming Omar Okribelashvili, Saba Meparishvili, Davit Koldari, Giorgi Kuchuashvili, Giorgi Okmelashvili, Fridon Bubuteishvili, Isako Devidze and Anatoli Gigauri. "All the individuals named by Gvaramia were found guilty by national courts. Three of them fully admitted to committing the crimes: Saba Meparishvili, Omar Okribelashvili and Davit Koldari," Gorduladze said. The committee chair also cited statements made by Giorgi Gakharia, leader of For Georgia, in April and May 2024. Gorduladze said Gakharia had described the protests at the time as peaceful and called on Georgia's international partners to adopt a unified position on the political developments in the country. Gorduladze quoted Gakharia's May 1, 2024, statement, in which he criticized the use of force against protesters: "This was exemplary punitive violence, the trail of which this time leads openly and directly to Ivanishvili, whose aim is to intimidate citizens. Ivanishvili deployed illegitimate force against peaceful protesters." Gorduladze also cited Gakharia's May 8 statement, in which he criticized the government for drawing parallels between the violent events of June 20, 2019, and the ongoing peaceful protests. He also referred to a July 9, 2024, statement by Natia Mezvrishvili, deputy chair of For Georgia, who called on the government to extend its announced amnesty to individuals prosecuted, fined or detained for what she described as nonviolent protests. During his remarks at the Constitutional Court, Gorduladze also presented statements by United National Movement leaders Mikheil Saakashvili and Tinatin Bokuchava. He recalled Saakashvili's April 25, 2024, message to young protesters: "I am proud of each and every one of you. You are all stronger than any of us." Gorduladze also cited Saakashvili's May 1 statement, in which he referred to the need for individual engagement with special forces officers and said victory was "within arm's reach." The committee chair further referred to a July 26, 2024, statement by Tinatin Bokuchava, in which she expressed readiness to stand surety for young people detained during the protests. Bokuchava said they were being punished for fighting to protect Georgia's European future. Gorduladze also cited statements by Federalists leaders Tamar Chergoleishvili and Giga Bokeria concerning Lazare Grigoriadis. He said Chergoleishvili had publicly supported Grigoriadis on April 29, 2023. On April 12, 2024, after Grigoriadis was found guilty by a court, she stated that he was innocent and that the state had no evidence against him. Gorduladze also recalled statements made by Giga Bokeria on March 30, 2023, and April 8, 2024. Bokeria described Grigoriadis' arrest as selective justice and referred to him as a symbol of the changes needed in Georgia's political system. The remarks were made during a Constitutional Court hearing on a lawsuit seeking to ban five opposition parties. Archil Gorduladze presented past public statements by opposition leaders concerning the 2023 and 2024 protests as part of the proceedings.

Vukovar Remembers 1991 Victims as Croatia Renews Call for Serbia’s Cooperation
articles.summary: Tens of thousands join annual Remembrance Procession, as Croatian officials urge Serbia's new government to provide information on fate of people still missing from 1991–1995 war.
articles.body: This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp Tens of thousands of people from across Croatia, neighbouring Bosnia and Herzegovina and other countries made their way through the streets of Vukovar on Wednesday as part of the annual Remembrance Procession in the eastern Croatian city, carrying national flags and other symbols, paying tribute to the defenders and civilians who died during the attack on the city in the autumn of 1991. “Everything has been rebuilt, but the wounds remain deep, as we are still searching for more than 300 of our fellow citizens. We will not find peace until we locate them,” Vukovar Mayor Marijan Pavlicek said. Citizens in procession wore T-shirts with the names of the fallen residents of Vukovar. Photo: V.Tesija/BIRN Vukovar’s wartime hospital staff led the procession this year. Of more than 1,000 people working there before the aggression started, only around 250 remained alive when the city fell under occupation. On November 20, 18 members of the hospital staff were killed at Ovcara farm near the city, alongside 182 other victims. The Siege of Vukovar was the bloodiest battle of the Croatian War of Independence. The city was razed to the ground by artillery attacks that lasted for three months, and following the collapse of its last defences, mass killings of prisoners and the wounded from the hospital took place. However, those three months bought time for Croatia to organise its defence against the Yugoslav People’s Army, JNA, which served as an instrument of Slobodan Milosevic’s regime in Belgrade. This secured Vukovar its heroic status in the creation of the modern-day Croatian state. Many young people, as well as families with children, took part in the procession; Vukovar, November 18, 2026. Photo: V.Tesija/BIRN Many participants in the Remembrance Procession were carrying Croatian flags and emblems representing the towns and places they come from, including Livno, Trogir, Pokupsko and Gospic. Entire families with young children, as well as large numbers of young people, also took part. The country’s officials also joined the procession, including President Zoran Milanovic, Parliament Speaker Gordan Jandrokovic and Prime Minister Andrej Plenkovic. Citizens arrived draped in national flags. Photo: V.Tesija/BIRN Speaking from Vukovar, Plenkovic reiterated that Croatia would not compromise on its demands towards Serbia and Montenegro in their EU accession processes. He said Croatia’s expectations were clearly defined and that both countries were expected to resolve issues. “It is important that we wait for the [Serbian] government to be formed, along with the relevant ministries and ministers who will address this issue,” Plenkovic told N1 television from the Remembrance Procession, referring to the new Serbian administration and Croatia’s expectations regarding the fate of the 1,725 people still missing from the Croatian war. He said there were people who knew where human remains had been relocated, but that Croatia had so far received insufficient information from Serbia about the missing. Banner reading “Croatia above all”. Photo: V.Tesija/BIRN Asked whether Zagreb might block the EU accession processes of Serbia and Montenegro if its demands were not met, Plenkovic ruled out any concessions. “As for Serbia, the number of missing persons is much higher. Regarding Montenegro, we have identified 14 individuals from the southern front in 1991. However, with regard to Serbia, expectations of the new administration have been heightened once again,” he said. “There will be no concessions. We have stated our expectations quite clearly. They know exactly what we expect,” he said. Reflecting on Vukovar’s sacrifice during the Homeland War, Plenkovic said that at a recent conference in Paris he had reminded European leaders that Vukovar was the first European city since 1945 to be virtually razed to the ground. “The Croatian people will never forget this sacrifice and the role played by Vukovar,” he said. Members of the association of Srebrenica genocide survivors also came to Vukovar. Photo: V.Tešija/BIRN Minister of Defence Ivan Anusic said in Vukovar that Serbia must provide documents about those who went missing and undergo a catharsis concerning its crimes and criminal policies from the 1990s. “Let them provide the documents regarding those who went missing during the Homeland War, and then perhaps we can begin to discuss something. Until then, it makes no sense,” Anusic said.

articles.title: Inside Kazakhstan’s new AI-powered public service centers
articles.summary: Kazakhstan has opened nine digital Public Service Centers (PSCs) where visitors can access government services independently with the help of eGov GPT, an AI-powered assistant. The Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development plans to expand the new format to regional centers across the country.
articles.body: Kazakhstan has opened nine digital Public Service Centers (PSCs) where visitors can access government services independently with the help of eGov GPT, an AI-powered assistant. The Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development plans to expand the new format to regional centers across the country. Unlike traditional PSCs, the new digital offices do not have a centralized queue for service operators. Instead, visitors can use self-service terminals or computers to select and apply for the government services they need. If they have questions, visitors can turn to eGov GPT. The AI assistant helps them identify the appropriate service, explains the next steps and guides them through the application process. Self-service areas account for 70% of each center’s floor space. Another 20% is dedicated to consultations with staff, while the remaining 10% is reserved for training areas where visitors can learn how to use digital services. Despite the shift toward self-service, consultants are available at every center to help visitors who have difficulty completing procedures on their own. «Services are becoming simpler, faster and more convenient for every citizen. At the same time, protecting personal data remains our absolute priority,» said Zhaslan Madiyev , Kazakhstan’s deputy prime minister and minister of artificial intelligence and digital development. The government also plans to introduce 24/7 document pickup through automated parcel lockers. The ministry has not yet announced a timeline for implementing the service. The first digital office opened in June 2026 in Zhezkazgan. Eight more have since opened in Astana, Shymkent, Turkestan, Satpayev, Uralsk, Petropavl, Karaganda and Taraz. According to the ministry, more than 90% of government services are now available online . In recent years, the number of requests handled by PSC operators has declined by 30%. Even when visiting a center in person, more people are choosing to complete service procedures themselves rather than rely on an operator. As previously reported by Kursiv.media , the government plans to retain only two or three operator workstations at each PSC. Employees at these stations will handle services that are not yet available online or cannot be completed independently. At the time, Rostislav Konyashkin , then a vice minister of digital development, assured the public that the changes would not result in mass layoffs. Some employees would transition to consulting roles, helping visitors navigate digital services, while others would be retrained to work on improving and simplifying government service procedures.

Meeting of the Strategic Committee for Weapons, Ammunition, and Mine-Explosive Ordnance Held
articles.summary: The 29th session of the Strategic Committee for Weapons, Ammunition, and Explosive Ordnance (Strategic Committee for NMiMES) was held today in Sarajevo. The session was co-chaired by the Deputy Minister of Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Slaven Galić, and the Chief of the Joint Staff of the Armed Forces of BiH, Lieutenant General Gojko Knežević—joined […] The post Meeting of the Strategic Committee for Weapons,…
articles.body: The 29th session of the Strategic Committee for Weapons, Ammunition, and Explosive Ordnance (Strategic Committee for NMiMES) was held today in Sarajevo. The session was co-chaired by the Deputy Minister of Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Slaven Galić, and the Chief of the Joint Staff of the Armed Forces of BiH, Lieutenant General Gojko Knežević—joined by his deputy, Major General Mirsad Ahmić, and international partners in BiH—with support from the OSCE Mission to BiH. According to a statement from the Ministry of Defence of BiH, the session addressed the implementation of activities regarding the disposal of surplus weapons, ammunition, and explosive ordnance (NMiMES); the progress of projects led by the UNDP in BiH and the OSCE Mission to BiH; support provided by EUFOR; infrastructure projects aimed at enhancing safety and security; as well as current challenges and future activities. In his opening remarks, Galić expressed special gratitude to the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in BiH, which hosted the session. He noted that, since the last meeting, progress has been made in addressing surpluses, modernizing storage facilities, improving storage conditions, and developing the competencies of personnel directly involved in these tasks. He emphasized that the true value of this process “is reflected in the extent to which we have succeeded in establishing a reliable system, reducing risks, enhancing accountability in the handling of stockpiles, and ensuring that these assets are managed in accordance with their condition, intended purpose, and applicable standards.” He highlighted the contribution of international organizations and partner countries—Austria, Norway, Germany, Sweden, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, and the United States—as well as their representatives, whose support has been significant to the progress achieved thus far. Cooperation with the UNDP, the OSCE Mission to BiH, EUFOR, NATO Headquarters Sarajevo, and other partners has extended beyond support for project implementation to include knowledge transfer, expert advice, training, and capacity development. Viktor Munteanu, Deputy Resident Representative of the UNDP in BiH, expressed his gratitude to the Ministry of Defence and the Armed Forces of BiH, as well as other participants involved in the implementation of the “Master Plan”—which covers the organization and training of personnel, the storage of assets, and the destruction of surplus/obsolete materiel within the Armed Forces of BiH. He commended the substantial progress made in constructing facilities for the safekeeping and storage of conventional ammunition and explosive ordnance (NMiMES) and noted that the implementation of the Master Plan has entered its final, third phase, which is scheduled for completion by the end of 2027. Major General Mirsad Ahmić, Deputy Chief of the Joint Staff of the Armed Forces of BiH (AF BiH) for Resources, presented activities regarding the reduction of surplus weapons, ammunition, and explosive ordnance (WAEO). He stated that, so far in 2026, the AF BiH has destroyed 78 tons of surplus WAEO, representing 61 percent of the quantity planned for this year. He noted that, with significant assistance from the Government of the Federal Republic of Germany and the UNDP, the infrastructure for the storage and safekeeping of weapons, ammunition, and explosive ordnance—as well as other infrastructure within the AF BiH—has been substantially improved. Significant results have also been achieved in personnel training regarding the handling and storage of weapons, ammunition, and explosive ordnance, as well as training in their safe handling. He specifically highlighted a course on ammunition life-cycle management, which was conducted with the participation of instructors from the UK and supported by a Swiss-Norwegian Mobile Training Team (CHE/NOR MTT). He further noted that the development of integrated information systems for the management and storage of weapons, ammunition, and explosive ordnance has progressed significantly. This, along with the aforementioned efforts, enhances the handling, storage, and disposal of such items, while improving the safety of AF BiH personnel and the broader community in BiH. Brigadier Martin F. Teachsler, Senior Advisor for the BiH Master Plan on Weapons, Ammunition, and Explosive Ordnance (WAEO), also addressed the meeting. He noted that the Master Plan concludes at the end of 2027, and that all necessary measures must be taken by then to ensure its full implementation. He commended the progress achieved through the sale of weaponry—an effort that required significant engagement from the Ministry of Defence and the Armed Forces of BiH. At the same time, he expressed dissatisfaction regarding the failure to resolve the issue of the remaining KUB surface-to-air missile systems, emphasizing that this must be a priority task. He pointed out that addressing the disposal of ammunition, weaponry, and secondary raw materials—generated through the demilitarization of ammunition, mines, and explosive ordnance (MiMES)—would significantly improve safety for personnel working at storage sites. He also touched upon the progress made regarding the involvement and work of Ministry of Defence personnel focused on explosive ordnance disposal (EOD) and environmental protection. Furthermore, he expressed hope that by the next meeting of the Strategic Committee for Ammunition, Mines, and Explosive Ordnance (NMiMES), scheduled for March 2027, there will be significant improvements in both the storage conditions for these items and the working conditions for the personnel tasked with managing them, the Ministry of Defence of BiH stated.
